design_rationale:
DESIGN RATIONALE / WORKLOG - task 1 (project_waitlist_reservations, env_0082) - revision 2

0. DRAW (draw_counts.py --task 1, fixed): prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[6, 5, 6, 4]. Root waitlist_ext_addon_offer_estimate 6, waitlist_ext_standard_offer_estimate 6, waitlist_ext_standard_request_fit 5, waitlist_ext_addon_request_fit 4.

1. WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. Henrik Sorensen asks only "can I finally get my add-on at Rondout Valley?". Rondout Valley has 6.40 kW open. The add-on offer rule waits on two states: (a) "An add-on offer and its estimate are fixed only after the add-on's requested kW is no more than the add-on fitted size of its utility account." (his add-on cc8f303b-42bb-4047-8f0f-98b881366f37 asks 1.30 kW; the fitted size of the house account is 1.2) and (b) "An add-on offer is made only after no Residential Standard reservation on the same project that can receive a valid offer is left in queued status." (his own cottage reservation 5313b50d-4abf-462c-9890-d35bfe9163f0, rank 3, is queued on the same project and can receive a valid offer). (b) leads to the Standard offer rule, which waits on its own fit: "A Residential Standard offer and its estimate are fixed only after the reservation's requested kW is no more than the standard fitted size of its utility account." (2.40 kW vs 1.8). Four problems: two customer-submitted fits (owner=user) and two offers, figured from waitlist offers, the house share f7b6d4c8-8219-434a-abc6-62a993bef0bf on Rondout Valley and the cottage share adfc6919-9cee-46d1-8874-31c39c6d9b12 on Wallkill River.

2. SCOPE / HEADROOM. Task 0 holds the Relocation Priority class; task 1 the Residential Standard and Residential Add-On classes. Each fit's scope requires the request so set to be within the account headroom (cottage: (6700 - 3.50 x 1140)/1170 = 2.3 kW; house: (10900 - 8.00 x 1170)/1170 = 1.3 kW), so no fit states a headroom term of its own. The Standard offer scope requires the reservation's utility account to hold no more than one active Residential share (the account share is then unique).

3. DSL ROUTE. Estimates rest on the household share's own statements and true-ups (projects and utility_accounts are unreadable); fits read the account share's true-ups and statements and this reservation's own offers on its project (the DSL scopes own-category reads to the reservation, and the rule words say "this reservation"). Every other case stays under the base rule (self-naming kWh and savings overwrites with sibling tails; no offered_kw overwrite).

4. FACTOR CARD.
 waitlist_ext_standard_request_fit (requested_kw 1.8; all-baseline 2.4). Order: usage replacement then margin; existing replacement then kept share; target replacement; room, then sizing.
  - usage_figure_averaging (parameter): three cottage true-ups in 36 whole months (5950, 6000, 6200) -> 6050; latest only -> 2.0.
  - banking_margin (parameter): two banked cottage lines in 12 whole months (one to three) -> x0.95; x1 -> 2.1.
  - existing_output_basis (method): latest cottage true-up shortfall 43 -> its credited 3035; expected 3078/0.90 -> 1.5.
  - existing_kept_share (method): no resize; subscriber_increase 0.50 kW effective 2026-09-01 since the 2026-06-16 review -> x 3.50/3.00; x1 -> 2.3.
  - target_yield_source (parameter): this reservation's latest offer on its project 2026-06-16 -> 2106/1.80/1 = 1170; twelve-month 8813/8.00 -> 2.0.
  plain: room = (6050 x 0.95 - 3035 x 1.166667)/1170 = 1.8860 -> 1.8; lesser of 2.40 and 1.8.
 waitlist_ext_standard_offer_estimate (savings 34.42; all-baseline 35.47).
  - output_history_basis (method): house true-up 2025-12-16 (10 whole months) -> 8209; twelve-month 8813 -> 35.92.
  - guarantee_output_floor (parameter): latest shortfall 215, contract year 1 none -> floor (8209 + 8424)/2 = 8316.5; none -> 34.10.
  - young_share_blend (parameter, MULTI-SOURCE): 35 posted lines, guarantee assessed -> 0.75 x 1039.5625 + 0.25 x 1170 = 1072.171875; unblended -> 33.37.
  - credit_value_recency (method): 10 whole months -> 1007.69/7824 = 0.128795; twelve-month -> 34.14.
  - credit_rate_trend (parameter, R6): contract-year-1 true-up 22 whole months ago -> x 0.1250/0.1225 = 1.020408; x1 -> 33.71.
  - banked_value_allowance (parameter, R6): cottage account share two banked lines -> half of 24.22/3011 = 0.004022; none -> 35.51.
  plain: kWh = RND(1.80 x 1072.171875) = 1930; savings = RND(1930 x (0.128795 x 1.020408 - 0.004022) x 14/100) = 34.42.
 waitlist_ext_addon_request_fit (requested_kw 1.2; all-baseline 0.9).
  - usage_figure_averaging (parameter): two house true-ups in 24 whole months, fewer than three in 36 -> (11150 + 10360)/2 = 10755; latest only -> 0.9.
  - banking_margin (parameter): four banked house lines -> x0.90; x1 -> 1.3.
  - existing_output_basis (method): house true-up shortfall 215 -> credited 8209; expected 8424/0.90 -> 0.2.
  - target_yield_source (parameter): this reservation's latest offer 2026-07-21 -> 936/0.80 = 1170; twelve-month 8813/8.00 -> 1.3.
  plain: room = (10755 x 0.90 - 8209)/1170 = 1.2568 -> 1.2; lesser of 1.30 and 1.2. No kept-share ladder is declared or stated in this rule.
 waitlist_ext_addon_offer_estimate (savings 22.91; all-baseline 25.33): same household figures as the Standard offer (per kW 1072.171875, value 0.128795, trend 1.020408); banked allowance full (four banked house lines) 112.49/8813 = 0.012764; kWh = RND(1.20 x 1072.171875) = 1287; savings = RND(1287 x 0.118659 x 15/100) = 22.91. Sensitivities: history 23.89, floor 22.69, blend 22.20, recency 22.70, trend 22.40, banked 25.37.
 Every factor is cross-difficulty (home).

5. FACTOR-READS TABLE: usage_figure_averaging -> account true-ups in 36 / 24 whole months (usage_kwh_12m); banking_margin -> account statements in 12 whole months (banked_value); existing_output_basis -> account latest true-up shortfall / credited, account twelve-month statements; existing_kept_share -> account latest true-up resize_kw, subscriber_increase filings since its review_date; target_yield_source -> this reservation's offers on its project (count in 12 whole months, latest date, larger kW, larger kWh), household latest true-up date / credited; offer factors as in task 0 plus banked_value_allowance -> account share statements (banked lines, banked value, net kWh). No factor reads another factor's binding.

6. DEFINING-SENTENCE TABLE: usage room / fitted size / usage figure / existing output / target yield / request set -> fit B1-B5; order -> fit and offer order sentences; whole months -> month sentences; each factor -> its own sentence; offer quantities -> offer B1-B6; account share and household share -> scope sentences.

7. PAIRWISE METHOD-TIER TABLE (B1): existing_output_basis T1 review credited_kwh_12m / T2 twelve-month statements / T3 review guaranteed over plan pct - review field vs statements vs review guarantee with plan param. existing_kept_share T1 allocation over allocation + resize_kw / T2 allocation over allocation less increase filings / T3 x1 - review field vs filings. Offer method tiers as in task 0. usage_figure_averaging is a parameter (value selected by how many true-ups fall in the window); target_yield_source is a parameter whose tiers read distinct records (own offers / household review / household statements) and never coincide on this world.

8. PROBES (probe_r2.py): later offer on the project to ANOTHER reservation -> add-on fit unchanged (reservation-scoped); later offer to this reservation on another project -> unchanged (project filter); same-date second offer with smaller kW -> unchanged, with larger kW -> it is taken (tie rule: larger offered_kw, then larger kWh); no offer within 12 whole months -> target tier 2; closed prior share on the cottage account -> unchanged (status filter); increase effective before the review -> not counted (kept x1); subscriber_decrease since review -> not counted; house share with one true-up -> averaging off; notice_given share on the cottage account -> Standard offer unchanged (active filter); cottage share never banked -> allowance 0; earlier true-up 24-35 whole months ago -> trend tier 2. Order replay through the task tools: gold order, add-on fit first and add-on fit second give one DB hash.

9. TRIGGER LIST: both offer tools write waitlist_offer_extended (-> waitlist_offer_made only) and waitlist_offer_made (-> []); both fit tools write waitlist_request_updated (-> []). waitlist_offer_accepted is never written.

10. PROBLEM TREE. Root waitlist_ext_addon_offer_estimate <- waitlist_ext_addon_request_fit (value_input, offered_kw) and <- waitlist_ext_standard_offer_estimate (state_gate, waitlist_reservations.status: no Standard reservation on the project that can receive a valid offer is left in queued status); waitlist_ext_standard_offer_estimate <- waitlist_ext_standard_request_fit (value_input). False at the opening: the add-on requests 1.30 vs 1.2; the cottage reservation is queued and requests 2.40 vs 1.8. Deletion sensitivity: without the add-on fit savings 24.81; without the Standard offer the cottage stays queued; without the cottage fit the Standard offer prices 2.40 kW at 45.89. The two branches touch disjoint rows and no computation reads a row the other branch writes (verified by replay). user_scenario names no prerequisite.

11. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Offers: offered_only (status set by the same call), queued status and class order (Standard rank 3 before Add-On rank 4; the add-on's earlier partial offers were each made when open capacity was below the Standard min_offer_kw 1.5, so the queued Standard reservation was passed over under the base rule), headroom on the offer date (2.3 and 1.3 kW cover 1.8 and 1.2), respond_by 2026-10-27 + 14 = 2026-11-10. Fits: request_changes (queued; decreases keep queue_date) and headroom.

12. SEED NOTES. Home charges at credit_value x (100 - 15|14)/100 half-up, consolidated, utility remittance; true-ups per the home true-up rule (guaranteed = allocation x 1170|1140 x 0.90; house CY2 shortfall 215, cottage CY4 shortfall 43 -> guarantee credits; no oversize); cottage increase request received 2026-07-14, filed for 2026-08, effective 2026-09-01 (within the cottage account sizing: 3.50 x 1140 = 3990 <= 6700). Own-category history under the extended rules: the eight seeded offers are partial (below requested_kw, at least min_partial_offer_pct and min_offer_kw), outside the extended full-offer scope, priced by the base rule (kWh = kW x 1170 rounded, savings = kWh x 0.1235 x plan pct), declined without penalty; queue-position notices every 6 months after queue_date and reconfirmation notices 30 days before each yearly due date are seeded for both reservations.

13. REALISM TAGS. R5: guarantee floor, shortfall-based existing output. R3: whole-month windows. Real sizing basis: expected production (guaranteed over plan pct) and the project's expected yield as quoted on this reservation's offers, as home_agg_account_sizing measures it. R6 (catalogue in worklog): banking margin and banked allowance, young-share blend weights, single-shortfall midpoint floor, credit-rate trend.

14. STANDARD SOLUTION + VERIFICATION. Reads (20), then Henrik's cottage fit (1.8), the Standard offer (1.80 kW, Commit 10, 1930 kWh, 34.42, 2026-11-10), Henrik's add-on fit (1.2), the add-on offer (1.20 kW, Commit 20, 1287 kWh, 22.91, 2026-11-10). Verification by check_compute's own evaluator (ev_t1.py) and gates 7/7 OK.

15. DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. Cottage: ((5950 + 6000 + 6200)/3 x 0.95 - 3035 x 3.5/3)/(2106/1.8) = 1.886 -> 1.8. House: ((11150 + 10360)/2 x 0.90 - 8209)/(936/0.8) = 1.257 -> 1.2. Per kW 0.75 x (8209 + 8424)/2/8 + 0.25 x 8424/8/0.9 = 1072.17; Standard 1930 kWh x (1007.69/7824 x 0.1250/0.1225 - 24.22/3011/2) x 0.14 = 34.42; add-on 1287 x (0.131424 - 112.49/8813) x 0.15 = 22.91. Same as gold.

16. REVISIONS. Round 1: reservation-scoped own-offer reads; null FK ids; every seeded row read. Round 2 (policy audit): target-yield words say "this reservation", with a same-date tie rule; state gate worded on queued status and on reservations that can receive a valid offer (base pass-over kept); prerequisite sentences match their conditions (fitted size); order sentences in both fits; headroom moved into the fit scopes; guaranteed-output sizing and share-keyed wear removed; guarantee floor tier 2 made live; kept share and credit-rate trend added; usage averaging labelled parameter; offered_kw overwrite removed (seeded partial offers now consistent with the charter); notices seeded; tool bodies enforce docstring formats; world re-tuned and every seeded row re-priced.
user_scenario:
You are Henrik Sorensen, a 68-year-old retired civil engineer in Kingston, New York. You are precise and courteous, and you like numbers explained plainly. You have a Meadowlark share on the Rondout Valley project for your house, and early last year you put in an add-on reservation to grow it a little; you have turned down a few small partial offers since. A neighbor told you Rondout Valley just freed up some space, so you are calling to ask: can I finally get my add-on at Rondout Valley? You want the representative to handle it on this call.
To confirm who you are you give your phone number 6515550172 and your ZIP code 12401; if more is needed, your date of birth is 1957-11-02. You don't have reservation or account numbers at hand. You also have a small Meadowlark share at your cottage in High Falls and a waiting-list reservation for the cottage on Rondout Valley; you mention these only if the representative asks about your other accounts or reservations.
If the representative explains that the add-on request has to be fitted to what your house's account can use before an offer can be made, you agree and tell them to set it to that fitted size; when they hand you the change to submit yourself, you submit it with exactly the size they give you. If they explain that your cottage reservation on the same project is ahead of the add-on in line and also has to be fitted to the cottage account first, you agree to that as well and submit that change yourself with the size they give you, and you are glad to hear the cottage can get its offer too.
When the representative tells you the offers have gone out - their sizes, plans, estimated first-year savings and the dates to answer by - you thank them, say you will read the offer letters and answer before those dates, and end the call. You do not accept or decline any offer on this call. If a figure doesn't match what you remember, you only ask them to check it against your records; you never propose a number.

edges.condition: The Residential Add-On reservation's requested_kw is no more than the add-on fitted size its utility account gives under the add-on fit rule.
edges.policy_source: An add-on offer and its estimate are fixed only after the add-on's requested kW is no more than the add-on fitted size of its utility account.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The add-on requests 1.30 kW but the add-on fitted size of the house account is 1.2 kW, so the add-on offer cannot be fixed.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Henrik's add-on fit sets requested_kw to 1.2; the add-on offer is figured on it.

edges.condition: No Residential Standard reservation on the add-on's project that can receive a valid offer under the base offer terms is in queued status.
edges.policy_source: An add-on offer is made only after no Residential Standard reservation on the same project that can receive a valid offer is left in queued status.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The cottage Residential Standard reservation on Rondout Valley is in queued status and can receive a valid offer (open capacity 6.40 kW, its fitted request within the cottage account headroom), so the add-on offer may not be made yet.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The Standard offer moves the cottage reservation from queued to offered with its written offer; no Standard reservation on the project is then left in queued status.

edges.condition: The Residential Standard reservation's requested_kw is no more than the standard fitted size its utility account gives under the standard fit rule.
edges.policy_source: A Residential Standard offer and its estimate are fixed only after the reservation's requested kW is no more than the standard fitted size of its utility account.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Two branches meet at the add-on offer: cottage fit -> Standard offer, and add-on fit. Their writes touch different rows (the cottage reservation and a new Standard offer row vs the add-on reservation). The add-on fit's target-yield factor reads only offers this reservation (the add-on) has received, in the rule's words ('where this reservation has received at least one offer on its own project') and in compute (reservation-scoped COUNT/LATEST/MAX), so the new Standard offer row on the same project is not one of its inputs; no other computation reads a row the other branch writes. Running the add-on fit before or after the cottage branch therefore gives the same terminal state and the same four figures (both orders replayed through the task tools). Within each branch the order is fixed by the prerequisite sentences: each offer waits on its own fit, and the add-on offer waits on no Standard reservation on the project being left in queued status.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the add-on fit the add-on offer is written on 1.30 kW: estimated_annual_savings 24.81 instead of 22.91, offered_kw 1.30 instead of 1.2, and the add-on's requested_kw stays 1.30.

Without the Standard offer the cottage reservation stays queued with no offer row (terminal waitlist_reservations.status queued instead of offered, one waitlist_offers row fewer) while the lower-ranked add-on is offered.
Without the cottage fit the Standard offer is written on 2.40 kW: estimated_annual_savings 45.89 instead of 34.42, and the cottage requested_kw stays 2.40.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only 'can I finally get my add-on at Rondout Valley?'. The cottage reservation is mentioned only if the representative asks about other accounts; fitting either request and the cottage coming first appear only as passive reactions beginning 'If the representative explains...'. No policy id appears.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: fit_standard_request_b636e3b6 and fit_addon_request_598035d1 write the requested_kw passed in; extend_standard_offer_cf280a13 and extend_addon_offer_d026003c write status offered and the offer row with the figures passed in, never checking fits, queue order or capacity (task_tools.py: one ctx.update / one ctx.create each). Offering the add-on first, on 1.30 kW, succeeds and records a wrong offer.
